decisions_made: Removed all 6 blanket suppressions in Interface.lean at once (rather than one at a time) per the Method's explicitly-sanctioned either-is-valid choice, then categorized the full 194-site warning surface from a single rebuild before fixing -- more efficient than 6 separate remove/rebuild/categorize cycles for a single-file target.

Used line-indexed Python scripts (read file, verify exact expected text at a given 1-indexed line number before replacing, write in one pass) instead of the Edit tool's string-uniqueness matching for the bulk of the style.longLine and unusedSimpArgs fixes. Several sites had textually identical tactic-call patterns (e.g. repeated `exact ⟨B', D, B'', ...⟩` closings across parallel Until/Since mirror branches, distinguished only by indentation or position) that the Edit tool's uniqueness requirement cannot disambiguate without brittle extra context; the line-indexed approach verifies against exact current content and fails hard on any mismatch, giving the same safety guarantee as Edit's matching without the ambiguity failure mode. Processed insertion-causing edits from the bottom of the file upward (or via single-pass whole-file rewrites) so that inserted lines never invalidated not-yet-processed target line numbers.

For style.show sites, verified the linter's exact reported column matched the start of the `show ` keyword before rewriting to `change ` at every one of the 74 sites, so that similarly-shaped term-mode `show ... from ...` expressions on the same or nearby lines (which the linter does not flag and must NOT be touched) were never accidentally rewritten.

For the one unusedSimpArgs site where the sole listed lemma was the unused one (`decreasing_by ... simp_all only [gt_iff_lt]`), rewrote to `simp_all only []` (an empty explicit-lemma list) rather than dropping `only` entirely, since the linter's own verification method (re-running simp without the flagged lemma and confirming no change in provability) establishes that `simp_all only []` is functionally identical to the original call minus the redundant lemma.

Verified the file is local-only (git cat-file -e upstream/main:<path> fails with exit 128) before editing, per the mandatory precondition; and verified live via direct removal that Interface.lean's declarations are public (not all-private), confirming it does NOT hit the sibling Elimination.lean's linter.privateModule (C7) permanent-exception category, rather than assuming symmetry.

Ran the full CSLib CI pipeline (all 8 steps except the cache fetch, already warm) once at cycle end, matching prior-cycle granularity -- the scoped rebuild plus downstream-importer rebuild plus full --wfail build already provided per-commit verification.

Committed the Lean file, the re-baselined ratchet file, and the plan update together in a single commit (fac20125), since this cycle closed exactly one file and the plan-update work was inseparable from recording that closure (unlike cycle 26's 9-file-plus-separate-plan-commit pattern).
